text:
marta_customer: Hey team — after our 23:00 deploy we're seeing a bunch of 401 invalid_api_key from the production service. Same key that worked yesterday. Example curl we use:

curl -i https://api.redwood.inference/v1/generate \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer k_************3xYz" \n  -d '{\"model\":\"redwood-1\",\"prompt\":\"hi\"}'

marta_customer: I originally copied the key from a notes app on my phone and pasted into our k8s secret during the rollback. Not sure if that matters.

sam_support: Hi @marta — thanks for the report. Can you paste the exact header you put in the secret (you can redact middle chars, just keep the first/last 4)? Also which client/library is calling the API?

marta_customer: Authorization: Bearer k_ABCdEFﬁghIJkLmnopQRsT   <-- pasted like this (i redacted)
marta_customer: Client is our internal node lambda using node-fetch. I did paste directly from iOS Notes.

julia_engineer: hmm that visible weirdness (looks like the letters around "EF" are squashed). Can you run this on the value you pasted and paste the hex output?

julia_engineer: ```bash
# replace <PASTED_KEY> with the value you put into the secret (keep quotes)
printf '%s' "<PASTED_KEY>" | xxd
```

marta_customer: ran it, output: `00000000: 6b5f 4142 43ef ac81 6768 494a 6b4c 6d6e  k_ABC....ghIJkLmnn`

julia_engineer: okay that's the smoking gun — bytes `ef ac 81` are the UTF-8 for the ligature U+FB01 (the "ﬁ" character). Looks like your phone's notes auto-replaced the substring "fi" with the single-character ligature. That means the key in the secret doesn't match the original ascii key.

julia_engineer: two options: 1) regenerate a new API key (we can rotate) and paste it from a plaintext source (desktop terminal) or 2) patch the secret by replacing the ligature with ascii "fi". Example quick fix (local):
```bash
# replace the ligature with ascii 'fi'
echo 'k_ABCdEFﬁghIJkL' | perl -CS -pe 's/\x{FB01}/fi/g'
```

sam_support: We'll rotate the key on our side and create a temporary key for you while you update the secret. For future: copy keys from password manager or a terminal, and if you ever paste from mobile check for substitutions.

marta_customer: Rotated and updated secret from my laptop — requests are green now, no more 401s. Thanks both :tada:

sam_support: Great — closing the loop. If you want, we can add a quick note in our troubleshooting KB about weird unicode substitutions when copying keys from phones.
